title: ORIC Pharmaceuticals Reports Inducement Grants under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
author: Na
description: ORIC Pharmaceuticals granted 125,400 non-qualified stock options and 20,550 restricted stock units to five new non-executive employees as inducement for employment. The grants were approved by the Compensation Committee and comply with Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4). The company continues development of its clinical-stage oncology candidates including rinzimetostat for prostate cancer and enozertinib for NSCLC.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The announcement is a routine corporate action regarding employee equity compensation. While it indicates company growth through new hires and ongoing clinical development (Phase 3 trial initiation, Bayer collaboration mentioned), the primary news is administrative in nature. No material clinical results, regulatory approvals, or significant business developments are disclosed that would warrant positive or negative sentiment.

title: INVESTOR ALERT: Pomerantz Law Firm Investigates Claims On Behalf of Investors of ORIC Pharmaceuticals, Inc.- ORIC
author: Pomerantz Llp
description: Pomerantz LLP is investigating potential securities fraud claims against ORIC Pharmaceuticals following a 41% stock price decline on March 31, 2026. The drop occurred after the company announced that its prostate cancer treatment (rinzimetostat/ORIC-944) performed roughly as effectively as competitors, falling short of expectations that it would be the best-in-class PRC2 blocker.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The company faces a securities fraud investigation following a significant 41% stock price decline due to disappointing clinical trial results for its flagship prostate cancer drug that failed to meet best-in-class expectations.

title: ORIC Pharmaceuticals Reports Inducement Grants under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
author: Oric Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
description: ORIC Pharmaceuticals announced equity inducement grants of 80,000 non-qualified stock options and 15,000 restricted stock units to a new non-executive employee hired in March 2026. The grants were approved by the Compensation Committee under Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4) and vest over time based on continued employment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article reports a routine equity grant to a new employee, which is standard HR practice for clinical-stage biotech companies. While the company continues development of its oncology candidates (rinzimetostat and enozertinib), the main news is administrative in nature with no material business developments, clinical trial results, or regulatory milestones that would warrant positive or negative sentiment.

title: ORIC Pharmaceuticals Stock Nosedives 25% After Hours: What Is Going On?
author: Tanya Rawat
description: ORIC Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: ORIC) surged 3.94% during regular trading but plummeted 24.86% in after-hours trading despite releasing positive Phase 1b clinical data for its lead drug candidate rinzimetostat in combination with darolutamide for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The treatment showed an 84% radiographic progression-free survival rate with favorable safety outcomes, and the company selected a 400 mg once-daily dose for Phase 3 trials expected to begin in H1 2026. The sharp after-hours decline suggests investor caution around early-stage results or profit-taking.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite positive clinical data showing 84% progression-free survival and advancement to Phase 3 trials, the stock experienced a significant 24.86% after-hours decline, indicating investor skepticism about the clinical results or concerns about valuation following the recent 120% year-to-date gain. The sharp sell-off outweighs the positive clinical developments.

title: Precision Killers: Why Big Pharma is Betting Billions to Beat a $170B Patent Cliff
author: Prnewswire
description: The precision oncology market is projected to grow from $110 billion to $225.65 billion by 2032, driven by Big Pharma's race to acquire registration-ready assets ahead of a $170 billion patent cliff through 2030. Several biotech companies are advancing promising clinical programs: Oncolytics Biotech strengthened its leadership team for pelareorep development in gastrointestinal cancers; Nurix is executing pivotal studies for its BTK degrader bexobrutideg in chronic lymphocytic leukemia; Erasca reported early clinical data for its pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015; Foghorn raised $50 million for its SMARCA4-targeting program; and ORIC presented strong Phase 1b data for rinzimetostat in prostate cancer.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company strengthened executive leadership with experienced oncology trial executives, advanced pelareorep toward registration with compelling clinical data (29-30% response rates in anal cancer, FDA alignment on pancreatic cancer Phase 3), and expanded scientific advisory board with top-tier cancer center experts.

Advanced BTK degrader bexobrutideg into pivotal Phase 2/3 development with strong clinical data (83% objective response rate in CLL), maintains solid cash position ($663.8 million), and is executing planned 2026 milestones for global registration.

Reported promising early clinical data for pan-RAS molecular glue ERAS-0015 with multiple confirmed responses at low doses, demonstrating potential differentiation from competitors, with Phase 1 data expected in H1 2026.

Successfully raised $50 million in equity financing at 30% premium, advancing Phase 1 trial for SMARCA4-targeting program, with selective CBP degrader program on track for IND in 2026 and cash runway extending to H1 2028.

Reported strong Phase 1b data for rinzimetostat in prostate cancer (55% PSA50 response rate, 59% ctDNA clearance) and enozertinib in lung cancer (67% ORR), with plans to initiate Phase 3 registrational trial in H1 2026 and extended cash runway to H2 2028.
